source.title: Learning and development in neural networks: the importance of starting small

confidence_rationale: Canonical origin of the 'staged development is necessary' position and the closest historical analogue to ARC-019's architectural commitment: a recurrent network trained on the full-complexity corpus from the start failed, while the same network succeeded when either the input or its own working memory was staged. Source quality is held down by its being a single 1993 simulation study on one artificial grammar with no replication reported in-paper, and by the fact that the central result was later directly contradicted (see the Rohde & Plaut 1999 entry in this directory). Mapping fidelity is moderate: Elman staged input complexity and memory span, not phase-advance on explicit competence criteria as ARC-019 specifies, and his comparison was staged-vs-full-from-the-start rather than matched-total-budget staged-vs-ungated. Aggregate weighted toward mapping_fidelity, as ARC-019 is an architectural commitment.
failure_signatures: The staged advantage in Elman (1993) was obtained under a comparison where the ungated control never traversed the task at all; an equivalent REE result would be indistinguishable from the V3-EXQ-591 substrate-ceiling non-result unless the non-degeneracy precondition is independently verified first.

Elman's gating variable was capacity/complexity of the input, not a competence criterion; a REE staged arm gated on DEV-NEED-008 criteria could reproduce his benefit purely by limiting effective input dimensionality early, with the explicit gate doing no work.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Networks trained on complex language tasks failed when fully formed but succeeded with limited initial capacity that gradually matured, suggesting developmental constraints may be necessary for mastering complex domains.
mapping.ree_translation: REE's staged developmental curriculum with phase-advance gates (InfantCurriculumScheduler, infant_substrate_expansion.md Section 8) is the same architectural bet: that a learner exposed to the full task from the outset fails to acquire structure that a progressively-scoped learner acquires, so the staging is load-bearing rather than merely organisational.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Elman's domain is next-word prediction over an artificial grammar in a small recurrent network with no reward, no embodiment and no policy; REE's is a multi-criterion embodied developmental gate. The transfer assumes the mechanism ('limited early capacity shapes what is learnable later') is domain-general, which is exactly what the subsequent literature disputes. Elman also did not equalise total training budget across arms in the way ARC-019's falsifier requires.
mapping.source_context: Simple recurrent network, artificial English-like grammar with embedded relative clauses, next-word prediction; 1993.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical and historically load-bearing, but a single un-replicated simulation whose headline result was contested within six years. Transfer risk elevated because the mechanism is claimed domain-general on the strength of one language-modelling task.
